items.title: Haywood Hillyer Interview, 1958-05-13
items.q: I heard for the first time, Pomp Selstein's band... we used to make a point of going to all the dances that they had, to hear Pomp Selstein.

ctx.x: It was prior to 1919 at the old French Opera House, because that's when the Opera House burned. And that would mean she went from her almost infancy back in the 70s, when everybody in the audience... But the one thing they did, they went to the Opera House, they lived in the Opera House, virtually. And the Opera House burned in 1919, if you know. And since then we've had opera, but not the opera that was the opera of 1840s down to 1919.

Thank you very much, sir. Okay, give me a name, please. My name is Lee Carroll. When were you born and where? I was born on October 11, 1938, in New Orleans. Have you lived in New Orleans all your life? No, I lived in Bay St. Louis, Mississippi, about 60 miles to New Orleans for seven years. From what age to what age would you say? From the age of... From the age of 10 to the age of 16. When did you first become aware of the intention of such a form of music as New Orleans jazz? Well, when I was about 12 years…
